questions_and_answers.question_text: What is Zhōng-Měi liǎngguó a formal way of saying?
What is the literal make-up of hézuò?
Give the three meanings of dìng.

answers.answer_text: To agree on; to draw up (a plan); to conclude (a treaty).
To carry, to transport, to ship.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What do hǎiyùn and kōngyùn mean?

answers.answer_text: Shipping by sea and shipping by air.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Explain how hé- can be used before other one-syllable verbs, with an example.
Translate into Chinese: We must work together on this if we are to do it well.
Translate into Chinese: These things are extremely heavy, and are difficult to transport.
Translate into Chinese: Let's put together a study plan!
Translate into Chinese: The equipment which was just shipped to Fújiàn is part of those plans.

articles.text:
11. A: Zhōng-Měi liǎngguó wèile zài gèfāngmiàn jìnxíng hézuò dìnghǎole bù shǎo jìhua.
   China and America have made a lot of plans to cooperate in various fields.
   B: Ǹg. Gāng yùn dào Fújiànde zhèixiē shèbèi jiù shi nèixiē jìhuàde yíbùfen.
   Mm. The equipment which was just shipped to Fújiàn is a part of those plans.

Notes on No. 11

Zhōng-Měi liǎngguó: "China and America, the two countries" This is a formal way of saying Zhōngguó hé Měiguó.

hézuò: "together-do," i.e., "to cooperate"

Wǒmen děi hézuò zhèijiàn shì cái néng bànde hǎo.
We must work together on this if we are to do it well.

Tā bú yào gēn wǒ hézuò.
He doesn't want to cooperate with me.

Xiànzài Zhōngguó hé wàiguó shāngrende hézuò yuè lái yuè duō le.
China is having more and more cooperation with foreign merchants.

Hé- can also be used before other one-syllable verbs, for example,

Zhèiběn shū shi wǒmen héxiěde.
We wrote this book together.

dìng: "to agree on; to draw up (a plan); to conclude (a treaty)"

Zánmen dìng ge xuéxí jìhua ba! Zhèiyang xiaqu, shénme yě xuébuhǎo.
Let's put together a study plan! We won't learn a thing if we keep on like this.

Yìbǎiduōnián qián, Qīngcháo zhèngfǔ hé wàiguó dìngle bù shǎo duì Zhōngguó hěn bù hǎode tiáoyuē.
More than a century ago, the Qīng Dynasty government concluded many treaties with foreign countries that were very bad for China.

yùn: "to carry, to transport"

Tā qù Zhōngguóde shíhou bǎ tāde qìchē yě yùn le.
When he went to China, he shipped his car over too.

Zhèixiē dōngxi fēicháng zhòng, yùnqilai bù fāngbian.
These things are extremely heavy, and are difficult to transport.

Zhème duō dōngxi, hǎiyùn bǐ kōngyùn piányide duō.
With so many things, it would be much cheaper to ship them by sea than by air.
